name: Rugra (Wild Mushrooms)
instructions: 1. Thoroughly clean the Rugra by soaking them in water to remove soil, then gently scrub and halve them.
2. Heat mustard oil in a pan until it smokes slightly, then add cumin seeds.
3. Add chopped onions and green chilies, sautéing until the onions turn golden brown.
4. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
5. Add turmeric, coriander powder, and red chili powder; mix well with a splash of water to prevent burning.
6. Add the cleaned Rugra mushrooms to the pan and coat them well with the spice mixture.
7. Cover and cook on low-medium heat for 10-15 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and release their moisture.
8. Finish with a sprinkle of garam masala and fresh coriander leaves before serving.
description: Rugra is a highly prized, seasonal delicacy found deep in the Sal forests of Jharkhand during the rainy season. It is often referred to as the 'truffle of Jharkhand' due to its rarity and rich, umami flavor. It holds immense cultural significance for the tribal communities of the region, marking the bounty of the monsoon season.
